t: Diodotus, satrap of Bactria, seceded from the Seleucid Empire around the middle of the 3rd century BCE; the exact date is unsettled, between a high chronology of c. 255 BCE and a low one of c. 246 BCE.
Under Demetrius, son of Euthydemus, the Bactrian Greeks invaded north-western India between 190 and 180 BCE, creating the Indo-Greek Kingdom.
The Bactrian language continued to be written in the Greek script until the 9th century CE, nearly a thousand years after the kingdom fell.
dyk: The Greco-Bactrians were the first in the world to issue coins of cupro-nickel, an alloy at the time known only to the Chinese; copper-nickel was not used again in coinage until the 19th century.
ev: Diodotus, Seleucid satrap of Bactria, secedes and becomes king; the date is disputed between c. 255 and c. 246 BCE
Euthydemus overthrows the dynasty of Diodotus II and founds his own
The Seleucid king Antiochus III attacks Euthydemus, who resists a three-year siege in Bactra
Antiochus III recognises Euthydemus and offers a daughter to his son Demetrius
Demetrius invades north-western India, founding the Indo-Greek Kingdom
Eucratides seizes power in a coup and founds the Eucratid dynasty
Eucratides is killed by his own son; Ai-Khanoum is burnt during nomadic invasions
The Yuezhi expand into Bactria and Heliocles moves his capital to the Kabul valley

f.capital: Bactra (also called Zariaspa); Heliocles later moved his seat to the Kabul valley
f.founder: Diodotus I Soter, Seleucid satrap of Bactria
f.successor: The Yuezhi, later the Kushan Empire; in the south the Indo-Greek Kingdom
